items.title: Features
items.text:
• Fully configurable – YAML-based configuration with environment variable overrides
  • Structured logging – JSON request tracing with request IDs and component tags
  • Liveness & Readiness probes – Kubernetes/Docker-compatible /health/live and /health/ready

items.text: Only the latest release of spikeball-league is supported with security updates. Users are encouraged to always upgrade to the most recent version.

items.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
items.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability, please report it via the GitHub Security Advisories page of this repository.

Do not disclose security issues publicly until they have been addressed.

We will review and respond to all reports as quickly as possible.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: We welcome contributions of all kinds — bug fixes, new features, documentation improvements, and more!

items.title: Before You Start
items.text:
• Read the Code of Conduct.
  • For security issues, follow the Security Policy — do not open a public issue.
  • For significant changes, open an Issue first to discuss your approach.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Go 1.24+
  • pre-commit (optional but recommended)

items.title: Clone & Run
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/Marcel2603/spikeball-league.git
cd spikeball-league

# Install dependencies and generate templates
go mod tidy
make generate

# Run the service
make run

items.title: Install Pre-Commit Hooks
items.text: make init-precommit

items.title: Workflow
items.text:
1. Fork the repository and create a feature branch from main.
  2. Make your changes, following the coding standards below.
  3. Write tests — we use table-driven tests and mock interfaces.
  4. Run the test suite: make test
  5. Run the linter: make lint
  6. Submit a Pull Request targeting main.

items.title: Coding Standards
items.text:
This project follows the Uber Go Style Guide.

Key rules:

  • Initialisms capitalised: UI, URL, ID, JSON, HTML
  • No panics — return errors, wrapped with %w
  • Pointer receivers for handlers
  • Functional Options for complex constructors
  • Always run make generate after editing .templ files

items.title: Semantic Commits
items.text:
We use Conventional Commits. PRs are merged via squash — only the PR title needs to follow the convention.

Prefix Effect feat: Triggers a minor release fix: Triggers a patch release chore: No release docs: No release refactor: No release BREAKING CHANGE: Triggers a major release

items.title: Database Behavior
items.text: The Spikeball League Tracker uses SQLite as its embedded database to store leagues, teams, players, and match history. This design ensures that the application remains entirely self-contained and easy to deploy without needing external database services like PostgreSQL.

items.title: Schema & Queries (sqlc)
items.text:
We use sqlc to generate type-safe Go code from SQL queries.

  • Schema: Defined in internal/db/schema.sql.
  • Queries: Defined in internal/db/queries.sql.
  • Generated Code: When you run sqlc generate (or make generate if configured), it generates the interface
  • Querier and the implementation in internal/db/.

This approach eliminates the need for reflection-based ORMs and catches SQL syntax errors at compile time.

items.title: Migrations
items.text:
Database migrations are managed using golang-migrate.

  1. Embedded Migrations: The SQL migration files are located in internal/db/migrations/ and are embedded directly into the binary using Go's //go:embed directive.
  2. Auto-Migration on Startup: When the application starts, db.NewDB(config) automatically applies any pending migrations. You do not need to run a separate migration script manually.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The database file location is fully configurable via the app.yaml configuration file (or via environment variables).

# app.yaml
database:
  path: "spikeball.db"

If the database file does not exist, SQLite will automatically create it upon first connection.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
When writing tests for handlers or database layers, you can use the special :memory: path to create a fast, isolated, in-memory SQLite database instance. This prevents tests from clashing on a physical file and guarantees an empty state for every test run.

Example usage for testing:

config := config.DatabaseConfig{Path: ":memory:"}
testDB, _ := db.NewDB(config)

items.title: Release
items.text: We use Github Action to release using semantic-release and goreleaser.

items.title: Strategy
items.text:
We release as needed, for example if we have added some rules or fixes any bug.

The release is currently manually and gets triggered by admins.

If you need to get a release, simply create an Issue or mention it in your pr.

items.title: ReleaseFlow
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant DeployWF as release.yml (orchestrator)
    participant ReleaseEnvironment as Environment
    participant ReleaseGate as release-actions.yml (reusable)
    participant SR as semantic-release
    participant GH as GitHub (Tags/Releases, GHCR)
    participant GR as GoReleaser

    Dev->>DeployWF: manual dispatch Release-Gate
    DeployWF->>ReleaseEnvironment: wait for approval
    Dev->>ReleaseEnvironment: Approve Deployment
    ReleaseEnvironment->>DeployWF: Start deployment
    DeployWF->>Release: uses: ./.github/action/action.yml
    Release->>SR: analyze commits (conventional commits)
    SR-->>ReleaseGate: decision (release? yes/no)
    alt New release
        SR->>GH: generate changelog + create tag + release
        ReleaseGate-->>DeployWF: outputs {released:true, tag:vX.Y.Z, version:X.Y.Z}
        DeployWF->>GH: checkout ref = tag
        DeployWF->>GR: build artifacts (binaries)
        DeployWF->>GH: publish release assets
        DeployWF->>GH: buildx + push Docker images to GHCR
    else No release
        ReleaseGate-->>DeployWF: outputs {released:false}
        DeployWF--x GH: skip build & push
    end

brew install spikeball-league

items.title: From Release
items.text: Download the latest binary from the Releases page and place it in your $PATH.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
The recommended way to run the service in production is via Docker:

docker pull ghcr.io/marcel2603/spikeball-league/spikeball-league:latest

Run with a custom config file:

docker run \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -v $PWD/app.yaml:/app/app.yaml \
  ghcr.io/marcel2603/spikeball-league/spikeball-league:latest

Or with custom branding assets mounted:

docker run \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -v $PWD/app.yaml:/app/app.yaml \
  -v $PWD/custom:/app/custom \
  ghcr.io/marcel2603/spikeball-league/spikeball-league:latest

items.title: From Source
items.text:
go install github.com/Marcel2603/spikeball-league@latest

This installs spikeball-league into your $GOPATH/bin or $GOBIN.

items.title: Start the service
items.text:
go mod tidy
make generate   # only needed once, or when framework versions change
make run

The service is now available at http://localhost:3000.

items.title: Overview
items.text: A lightweight, auth-less web application for tracking Spikeball leagues, teams, and match scores. The system prioritizes extreme ease-of-use via a "StrawPoll/Doodle" creation model, eliminating user registration while maintaining secure administrative control.

items.title: Techstack
items.text:
• Backend: Go (Golang)
  • Frontend: HTMX (hypermedia-driven interactions), Alpine.js (client-side state & UI tweaks)
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS
  • Templates: a-h/templ (type-safe HTML generation)
  • Database: SQLite (embedded, single-file database) with support for PostgreSQL
  • Deployment: Docker

items.title: Monitoring & Health
items.text:
• Metrics: The application exports Prometheus-compatible metrics.
  • Health Checks: Standard /health/live and /health/ready endpoints for container orchestration.

items.title: AuthLess Mode
items.text:
• To eliminate login friction, the application uses a token-based URL routing architecture rather than traditional sessions.
  • Public Link (/l/): Shared with the friend group. Used to view standings, match history, and submit new game scores.
  • Admin Link (/admin/): Kept strictly by the creator. Used to manage the league (rename, delete matches, edit players).
  • Client-Side Persistence: When an admin creates a league, Alpine.js intercepts the response and stores the admin_id and League Name in the browser's localStorage. The index page (/) reads this to provide a "Your Recent Leagues" shortcut for returning creators.

items.title: Static Assets
items.text: The documentation and certain frontend assets are pre-generated using internal tools and bundled or served alongside the Go binary to ensure a single-dependency deployment model.

items.title: Health Endpoints
items.text: The service exposes two dedicated health endpoints for use with container orchestrators and load balancers.

items.title: Liveness — GET /health/live
items.text:
Signals that the process is running. It has no external dependencies and always returns 200 OK.

GET /health/live

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"ok"}

items.title: Readiness — GET /health/ready
items.text:
Signals that the service is ready to serve traffic.

GET /health/ready

All fine reachable:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"ok"}

items.title: Log Behaviour
items.text: Both /health/live and /health/ready are excluded from application logs to prevent polling noise in production environments.

items.title: Kubernetes Example
items.text:
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/live
    port: 3000
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10

readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/ready
    port: 3000
  initialDelaySeconds: 3
  periodSeconds: 5

items.title: Docker Compose Example
items.text:
services:
  spikeball-league:
    image: ghcr.io/marcel2603/spikeball-league/spikeball-league:latest
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:3000/health/live"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

Tip: Use health/live for the Docker Compose healthcheck (lightweight). Use health/ready as the Kubernetes readiness probe so traffic is not routed until all external dependencies are reachable.

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
The service exposes a Prometheus-compatible /metrics endpoint to help you monitor the health, performance, and usage of the application.

This endpoint combines standard HTTP/application metrics with custom metrics specifically designed to track operation performance.

items.title: Endpoint Details
items.text:
• Path: /metrics
  • Method: GET
  • Format: Prometheus Text-based format (text/plain)

items.title: Custom Metrics
items.text:
To help monitor the performance and reliability of your server, the service exposes the following custom metric:

  • None

items.title: Version
items.text: The /version endpoint returns the current build version and commit hash of the running service.

items.title: Endpoint Details
items.text:
• Path: /version
  • Method: GET
  • Format: application/json

items.title: Response
items.text: Field Type Description version string The application version (e.g. v1.2.3) commit string The Git commit hash of the build

items.text:
{
  "version": "v1.2.3",

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The service is configured in layers, applied in this priority order (highest wins):

  1. cmd/config/app.default.yml – baseline defaults embedded in the binary
  2. app.yaml or app.yml – user-supplied overrides (optional)
  3. Environment variables – highest priority, useful for containers

See the sub-pages for the full reference of each configuration section.

items.title: What to configure
items.text: All options are nested under their respective top-level YAML keys. Below is a full annotated reference.

items.title: Server
items.text:
Controls the HTTP listener.

server:
  host: localhost   # Hostname used for CORS allowed origins
  port: 3000        # Port the service listens on
  domain: http://localhost:3000 # Domain to use for generated public links
Key Type Default Description server.host string localhost Allowed CORS origin hostname server.port string 8080 HTTP port to listen on server.domain string http://localhost:8080 Public domain prefix for generated URLs

items.title: Log
items.text:
Controls the log level.

log:
  level: info
Key Type Default Values log.level string info debug, info, warn, error

All logs are emitted as structured JSON to stdout with source file and request ID (req_id) fields attached.

items.title: Database
items.text:
Controls the local SQLite database connection.

database:
  path: spikeball.db
Key Type Default Description database.path string spikeball.db File path to the SQLite database.

items.title: YAML Files
items.text: The service merges configuration from two YAML files at startup:

items.title: app.default.yml
items.text: Bundled inside the binary — provides safe defaults. Do not edit this file directly.

items.title: app.yaml / app.yml
items.text:
Your user-supplied override file. Place it next to the binary (or mount it at /opt/spikeball-league/app.yaml in Docker). Only the keys you specify will take effect — the rest fall back to app.default.yml. The system will automatically detect either app.yaml or app.yml.

Example minimal app.yaml:

server:
  port: 8080

items.title: Environment Variables
items.text:
Every configuration key can be overridden via an environment variable. The variable name is derived by uppercasing the YAML path and joining segments with _.

YAML key Environment variable server.port SERVER_PORT server.host SERVER_HOST server.domain SERVER_DOMAIN log.level LOG_LEVEL database.path DATABASE_PATH

Example Docker run with environment variables:

docker run \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  ghcr.io/marcel2603/spikeball-league/spikeball-league:latest
